what: On a single no-scroll screen, cells (work videos etc.) are advanced one at a time with the wheel. The wheel is not passed on immediately but accumulated — one mouse wheel notch adds 125px, and trackpad deltaY × 2.5 clamped to ±35 pulls the panel up, and while not advancing the panel follows 10% of the remaining distance each frame. When the accumulated distance exceeds 30% of the cell height it advances to the next cell in 700ms (a mixed curve: power2.out at first, landing with expo.out at the end), and during that time and for 50ms after it ignores the wheel. If it fails to advance and rests 300ms, it returns to place with cubic in-out 620ms. The current cell is reported via --fx-index and fx:slide.

options.step: Distance of one mouse wheel notch (px), default 125
options.pass: Paging threshold (share of cell height), default .3
options.[data-fx-part=track·slide]: Animated panel · slot (direct child of the panel)
options.fx:slide: Event emitted by the element when the cell changes (detail.index)

from.where: index.js Stage — original IndexMain (qt 125 · Jn 2.5 · Xt 35 · Xn .3 · qn 300 · Wn .1 · Bn 700 · He 620)

note: Intercepts the wheel (preventDefault), used when a panel fills the whole screen. Touch devices don’t intercept and leave it to default scroll + cell snapping (css)
